title: Iran messaging shifts · what was said, what closed the lane, what came next
method: This is not a propaganda blacklist. It tracks changes between Iranian stated positions, outside acts, observable outcomes and later Iranian framing.
A changed position can be established from words and behavior. The reason for the change is a separate inference.
Labels such as walk-back cover, lane shift or compensating hardening are hypotheses with confidence levels, not findings about hidden intent.
Actor claims remain claims; regional or U.S. pressure is not treated as causal proof unless the sequence and evidence support that narrower conclusion.

R_JUL07.title: Ship hit in Hormuz; Iran says no talks unless Trump halts
R_JUL07.supports: Iranian public sequencing line that talks required Washington to halt coercive action/change course; also records U.S. retaliation and pressure.
R_JUL07.quality: HIGH for fact of statements/events; attribution remains source-bounded

R_AUG25_TALKS.title: Iran vows to retaliate after U.S. widens sanctions
R_AUG25_TALKS.supports: Iran expressed general willingness to resume talks through Pakistani mediation before the old MOU package had been restored; Pakistani-source account of possible U.S. sanctions reversal remained unconfirmed by Washington.
R_AUG25_TALKS.quality: HIGH; mediated U.S. sequencing claim remains unconfirmed

FT_AUG25_OMAN.title: Iran-Oman phased Hormuz framework
FT_AUG25_OMAN.supports: Joint Iran-Oman movement toward a temporary shared corridor, mine-clearing and future administration/services.

IR_MAY27.title: Hormuz control and nuclear sovereignty framed as inviolable red lines
IR_MAY27.supports: Iranian state-media strategic framing presented nuclear industry, Hormuz sovereignty, defense/asymmetric capabilities and the Axis as non-negotiable capital.
IR_MAY27.quality: IRANIAN STATE-MEDIA POSITION; establishes messaging, not independent fact

IR_JUN16.title: Iran VP says Tehran will maintain control of Strait of Hormuz
IR_JUN16.supports: Aref said management would remain Iran's responsibility and vessels should contribute to service costs.
IR_JUN16.quality: IRANIAN OFFICIAL POSITION VIA STATE MEDIA

R_AUG26_IRGC.title: Iran and Oman reach agreements on share of Hormuz and revenues, Revolutionary Guards say
R_AUG26_IRGC.supports: IRGC claimed control/revenue-sharing results while a senior Iranian source said details were not finalized.
R_AUG26_IRGC.quality: HIGH for fact of divergent Iranian statements; final terms unresolved

QAT_AUG25.title: Qatar-Iran foreign-minister call
QAT_AUG25.supports: Qatar backed the Iran-Oman technical process while explicitly requiring freedom of maritime navigation and a comprehensive agreement.

QAT_AUG26_SA.title: Qatar-Saudi foreign-minister coordination
QAT_AUG26_SA.supports: Qatar and Saudi Arabia coordinated on de-escalation; Qatar again stated support for a solution ensuring freedom of maritime navigation and a comprehensive agreement.

R_AUG27_QATAR.title: Qatar PM visits Tehran to pursue mediation efforts
R_AUG27_QATAR.supports: Qatar PM/FM met Araghchi in Tehran; Reuters preserves the split between IRGC claims of agreed control/revenues and an Iranian source saying details remain unfinished; Qalibaf used an economic-war frame.

R_AUG27_TRAFFIC.title: Shipping traffic through Strait of Hormuz rises slightly
R_AUG27_TRAFFIC.supports: Kpler visible traffic rose to 10 commodity vessels Wednesday from eight Tuesday, still below the recent average; AIS-dark traffic remains a limitation.

R_MOU_JUN17.title: 14-point U.S.-Iran Islamabad MOU
R_MOU_JUN17.supports: The interim MOU put final enrichment/inspection rules into a later final-deal process while imposing interim nuclear and maritime obligations.

IR_AUG26_NUCLEAR.title: Iran nuclear chief says attacked sites require a special inspection protocol
IR_AUG26_NUCLEAR.supports: Reports Mohammad Eslami saying struck nuclear sites cannot be inspected under ordinary procedures until a special protocol is established, while routine inspections continue at sites not attacked.
IR_AUG26_NUCLEAR.quality: ESTABLISHED IRAN-FOCUSED OUTLET; fact of reported official statement

R_AUG24_SANCTIONS.title: U.S. Treasury broadens secondary-sanctions pressure on Iran
R_AUG24_SANCTIONS.supports: Washington broadened counterparty economic pressure while using a cure-period approach rather than immediately sanctioning every major Chinese financial node.

series.issue: Return to talks / who must move first

said.speaker: Iranian leadership / officials
said.label: ASSERTIVE / LEGITIMIZING MESSAGE
said.text: Iran's public position was that Washington had to halt coercion and change course before talks could resume.

closing_acts.act: Broadened secondary-sanctions pressure rather than restoring the old MOU package.
Carried mediation between Washington and Tehran and publicly described progress toward a negotiated settlement.
Moved with Iran into a concrete phased Hormuz corridor and mine-clearing process.

occurred.label: OBSERVED REALITY
occurred.text: Iran validated Pakistani mediation and entered the Oman process before Washington restored the old blockade, sanctions, asset and reconstruction package it had demanded as the price of returning.

shifted_to.label: OPTIONALITY-PRESERVING / NEGOTIATING MESSAGE
shifted_to.text: Tehran moved to willingness to negotiate through mediators while preserving the claim that it was negotiating from strength and that U.S. coercion remained illegitimate.

assessment.classification: WALK-BACK IN PROCEDURAL PRECONDITION / FACE-SAVING LANE AVAILABLE
assessment.confidence: HIGH on movement; MEDIUM on narrative purpose
assessment.text: The walk-back itself is observable: Iran entered a political process before its stated precondition was met. Calling the new language deliberate cover is an inference, not a fact. It could also reflect changed policy, factional differences or mediator-created sequencing.

series.status: PRIMARY UNILATERAL LANE NARROWING / REGIONALIZED LANE ADVANCING

said.speaker: Iranian state/official messaging
said.label: ASSERTIVE / LEGITIMIZING MESSAGE
said.text: Iran framed Hormuz sovereignty/management as an Iranian red line and said Tehran would retain management responsibility while ships contributed to service costs.

closing_acts.act: Advanced a shared temporary corridor, joint mine-clearing and negotiations over future administration rather than unilateral Iranian rule.
Backed the Oman process but explicitly tied the acceptable end state to freedom of navigation and a comprehensive agreement.
Coordinated with Qatar on the regional de-escalation track while Qatar restated freedom-of-navigation terms.
Moved the regional pressure/mediation track into an in-person Tehran meeting.

occurred.label: OBSERVED REALITY
occurred.text: The operative process became shared and regional. Iran still has real gatekeeping leverage, but the reviewed record does not show recognized unilateral permanent control or an accepted compulsory Iranian toll regime. Visible traffic also began edging upward while negotiations continued.

shifted_to.label: OPTIONALITY-PRESERVING / NEGOTIATING MESSAGE
shifted_to.text: The IRGC reframed progress as agreement over Iran/Oman shares, control and revenues, while another Iranian source said the details were not finalized. That allows Tehran to describe a regionalized arrangement as recognition of Iranian rights without publicly saying it abandoned the earlier unilateral claim.

assessment.classification: LIKELY LANE SHIFT AS UNILATERAL RECOGNITION PATH NARROWS
assessment.text: The substantive change toward a shared framework is observable. The inference is that regionalization gives Tehran a way to cover the walk-back by claiming it resisted U.S. dictates and reached a Gulf agreement instead. Final terms remain unresolved, so Atlas does not yet call the unilateral demand definitively dead.

series.issue: Nuclear sovereignty / inspections as the next protected lane
series.status: LANE PROTECTION / SHIFT NOT YET COMPLETE

said.speaker: Iranian state-media strategic position
said.label: ASSERTIVE / LEGITIMIZING MESSAGE
said.text: Iran framed its nuclear industry and defense architecture as non-negotiable sovereign capital.

closing_acts.act: The interim MOU imposed interim nuclear obligations and placed the harder enrichment/inspection end state into final-deal negotiations.
Kept economic pressure active while the final nuclear bargain remained unresolved.
Tied Hormuz normalization to a broader comprehensive diplomatic agreement and then carried that mediation into Tehran.

occurred.label: OBSERVED REALITY
occurred.text: There is still no controlling final nuclear settlement. Iran has already accepted that nuclear terms can sit inside a final-deal process, but it is now hardening the inspection procedure for sites struck in the war.

shifted_to.label: ASSERTIVE / LEGITIMIZING MESSAGE
shifted_to.text: Nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami said attacked sites require a special inspection protocol before IAEA access, while routine inspections continue at unstruck sites.

assessment.classification: POSSIBLE COMPENSATING HARDENING / SOVEREIGNTY LANE PROTECTION
assessment.confidence: MEDIUM-LOW on motive; HIGH on reported position
assessment.text: This may be Tehran protecting a domestic red line while the Hormuz lane becomes more negotiable: concede or regionalize one issue while demonstrating it has not become generally pliable. That motive is not proven. The inspection stance could also be a genuine security/legal response to damaged wartime sites.
alternatives: bureaucratic policy rather than messaging strategy
